title: Experiment: use dashboard Task as authoritative command lifecycle
description: Determine whether the existing Amplify dashboard Task model can be the single authoritative command lifecycle record. Experiment only: add scalar lease, digest, fencing, idempotency, and cancellation fields to dashboard/amplify/data/resource.ts without adding a Command model, relationship, or index. Prove CloudFormation resource-count/replacement behavior, conditional claim and fencing semantics, and dashboard Task subscription updates. Restore experimental files after validation; do not modify command-worker production code.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Started disposable Amplify schema experiment. Scope is limited to dashboard/amplify/data/resource.ts plus temporary local test artifacts; no worker production code, deployment, commit, or PR.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Experiment complete. Baseline and six-field schema both synthesized data/amplifyData/ConnectionStack at 469 resources (delta 0); no logical resources were added/removed, Task key schema/GSIs stayed unchanged, and no replacement was indicated. Generated GraphQL exposed updateTask(condition: ModelTaskConditionInput) plus onUpdateTask. Live AppSync proof: claim A succeeded, concurrent claim B and stale fence update failed conditionally, cancellation settlement succeeded, post-cancel success was rejected, and onUpdateTask delivered the updated Task fields. Backend typecheck passed. Disposable sandbox and synthetic Tasks were deleted; resource.ts was restored with no diff.
